body: The company uses multiple debt sources to finance its acquisition of Japanese pharmaceutical firm MicroBiopharmIndian drugmaker Gujarat Themis Biosyn has secured private credit funding to support its acquisition of Japan-based MicroBiopharm Japan, as companies increasingly use private credit to finance overseas expansion. The company completed the acquisition of 100 per cent of MicroBiopharm Japan through its wholly owned subsidiary, Themis Biosyn Japan, for JYP 21.5 billion.Private Credit FundingGujarat Themis received JYP 9.2 billion, or about USD 58 million, in financing from Asian private credit fund Orion Capital Asia, according to people familiar with the matter. The people asked not to be identified because they were discussing non-public information.Gujarat Themis had announced the JYP 21.5 billion acquisition in May 2026. The transaction was funded through a combination of debt and equity and was completed after the required regulatory approvals and closing conditions were fulfilled.A spokesperson for Gujarat Themis was not immediately available for comment, while a representative of Orion Capital Asia declined to comment.Additional Debt RaisingBesides the Orion facility, Gujarat Themis raised Rs 585 crore through a private placement of secured five-year debentures, according to a 16 September company statement. The company said the proceeds would be used to invest in its wholly owned Japanese subsidiary to finance the acquisition and for general corporate purposes.The debentures included instruments carrying a coupon of 10 per cent and 18-month notes paying 17.75 per cent, according to the statement.Indian private credit funds managed by Avendus Capital and Edelweiss Alternatives purchased the rupee-denominated debt, according to the people familiar with the matter. A spokesperson for Avendus Capital said the fund was a lead investor in the debt, while Edelweiss Alternatives did not immediately respond to a request for comment.Gujarat Themis also invested Rs 475 crore as capital contribution and provided Rs 745 crore as a loan to Themis Biosyn Japan in connection with the acquisition, according to the company's 18 September disclosure.Private Credit Gains GroundAsian companies are increasingly turning to private credit to fund overseas expansion, as private lenders can provide financing outside traditional bank channels.A similar transaction took place earlier this year when Indonesian petrochemicals producer PT Chandra Asri Pacific tapped KKR's insurance business Global Atlantic to finance its USD 1 billion acquisition of Esso-branded service stations in Singapore from Exxon Mobil.Japan AcquisitionGujarat Themis acquired MicroBiopharm Japan from funds managed or advised by T Capital Partners Co., a Japan-based private equity fund. MicroBiopharm Japan has more than six decades of experience in fermentation, microbial-based research, development and pharmaceutical and specialty chemicals manufacturing. It operates three GMP-compliant manufacturing facilities.For FY26, MicroBiopharm Japan reported revenue of JYP 9.5 billion, according to Gujarat Themis' disclosure, with about 40 per cent of its revenue generated outside Japan.Founded in 1981, Gujarat Themis is an Indian pharmaceutical company involved in fermentation-based pharmaceutical intermediates and active pharmaceutical ingredients. The company has said it was the first in India to commence commercial production of Rifampicin.
